written.myAnswer: Temporary magnets lose most of their magnetism when the magnetising force is removed; permanent magnets retain their magnetism.
The region around a magnet in which its magnetic effect can be detected is called its magnetic field.
Magnetic lines of force are imaginary lines used to represent the direction and shape of a magnetic field.
Permanent magnets are used in loudspeakers and compasses. Electromagnets are used in electric cranes and circuit breakers.
Magnetic domains are tiny regions in a magnetic material in which the atomic magnets are aligned in the same direction.
A current-carrying long coil (solenoid) produces a uniform magnetic field inside it.
Paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted by a magnetic field, whereas diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by it.
The magnets are stored with unlike poles next to each other at each end, and P and Q are soft-iron keepers.

The facing poles must be like poles (N–N or S–S), with opposite poles at the outer ends. Their fields cancel at the midpoint, so the compass aligns with Earth’s field; the field lines bend away from the gap between the like poles.
Yes. A changing magnetic field can induce an electric current. For example, moving a magnet into or out of a coil changes the magnetic flux through the coil and induces current.

At the centre, the field due to each solenoid should point away from that solenoid. The four equal fields then cancel when all are on; switching one off leaves the other three with a resultant toward the switched-off solenoid.
Test for repulsion using a known magnet. Repulsion proves the object is itself a magnet; attraction alone does not distinguish a magnet from an unmagnetised magnetic material.

The field is strong where its lines of force are crowded closely together and weak where they are farther apart. Diagrams should show dense lines for a strong field and widely spaced lines for a weak field.

A circuit breaker is a safety device that automatically opens a circuit when excessive current flows. In an electromagnetic circuit breaker, the current energises an electromagnet, which attracts an armature and opens the contacts.
The statement is false. A magnet attracts magnetic materials and attracts the unlike pole of another magnet; like poles repel.

In domain theory, paramagnetic materials have atomic magnets that align weakly with an applied field, while diamagnetic materials develop a weak opposing magnetisation. Ferromagnetic materials contain domains that can align strongly, producing strong attraction.
Ferromagnetic materials are suitable for making magnets because their domains can align strongly, producing a large magnetic effect, and suitable materials can retain that alignment.
